rows.explainer: Total expenses $2,309,271k less the non-cash items in the functional expenses: donated goods distributed $1,918,357k, expired donated stock written off $250,458k, donated freight $1,648k and donated services $292k = $138,516k. rows.label: Defined daily doses of medicine delivered, fiscal 2025 (USA and international)

source.title: Direct Relief, Fiscal Year 2025 Annual Report (July 2024 to June 2025)
source.quote: 311,865,693 in Defined Daily Doses of medicine

rows.explainer: The WHO's unit of drug use: one DDD is one adult's assumed average daily dose of a medicine, so 365 DDD are about a patient-year of treatment. Direct Relief's own count (527 million the year before, p. 43).

rows.label: Years a gift to Direct Relief waits before it is spent

source.title: Direct Relief and Affiliates, Report of Independent Auditors and Consolidated Financial Statements, June 30, 2025 and 2024 (Baker Tilly, audited)
source.quote: Financial assets available to meet general expenditures over the next twelve months 183,256

rows.explainer: Financial assets available for general spending, $183.3m, are 1.3 years of cash spending ($138.5m: total expenses less donated goods, expired stock and donated freight and services, p. 6-8): the upper end. Gifts designated for a disaster (60% of cash support, annual report p. 38) are spent within months. Our estimate, 0.7 years.

rows.label: Share of the year's defined daily doses that went abroad
rows.explainer: Direct Relief doesn't split its doses by programme. Anchor: international partners got 84.5% of the material aid by value ($1,633m of $1,933m, annual report p. 43); US clinics get mostly generic medicines for chronic illness, which are cheap per dose, so their share of doses is above their share of value. Our judgment, 70%. It only splits the doses between the two models for the per-patient-year figures: the health gained comes from the goods' value, so the results don't move with it.
